messages:
Iris: quick follow-up from the dashboard pass  on narrow widths the chip group in the header feels stacked and the toast pops over it. thinking we should make chips collapse into a single overflow chip at <=360px instead of wrapping.
Tom: collapse into a +N chip sounds right. does that change keyboard navigation semantics? we need the overflow chip to open a menu with focus trapped to the chip group.
Keiko: agree. overflow chip should be keyboard focusable and announce its children with aria-expanded/aria-controls. also suggest the overflow label be "More filters" instead of just "+3" when space allows (aria-hidden vs visible label).
Jared: minor visual nit  when chips collapse the header height jumps slightly. can we keep header stable by reserving chip row height and animating opacity so layout doesn't shift when toast animates?
Iris: good point. propose: .header { min-height: var(--header-compact-h); } and chips toggle visibility with fade. toasts: move compact toasts to bottom-left on small screens to avoid header collisions.
Tom: about focus visuals: chip focus currently uses focus-ring-primary at 3px. on compact that looks heavy. recommend focus-ring-compact 2px with inner offset so chips don't feel bulky.
Keiko: accessibility reminder: when we move toasts, ensure they have role="status" and aria-live="polite" so screen readers skip rapid updates. also overflow chip menu should have aria-labels for each filter option.
ux-bot: accessibility scan queued. results: overflow chip menu needs accessible names. toast role/status recommendation applied. focus contrast checks pass at 4.5:1 for chip text on proposed background. recommendation: implement keyboard trapping for overflow menu and avoid focus loss when toast appears.
Jared: thanks. one last microcopy: the collapsed chip menu header currently says "Filters"  can we label it "Active filters" to clarify stateful controls.
Iris: will update figma: implement +N overflow chip with accessible label, add min-height to header to prevent layout shift, move compact toasts to bottom-left, and use focus-ring-compact for chip focus. i'll post the figma link when ready.
Tom: great, thanks iris.
Keiko: approved pending keyboard trapping test.
Iris: noted  will follow up with QA on trapping and toast placement.
